accepted.reason: One synthetic HTTP scope for the actual mounted action host: controlled historical clock, remote/unconfigured-request detection, canonical Core/Capiro defaults, action response queue, request/header ledger and exact entered/released/completed request barriers. Queue, ledger and barriers are coupled evidence of dispatch and lifetime behavior; they are not application orchestration, a duplicate receiver, an authorization implementation or unrelated mocks. The109-line function reuses existing operationFixtures/onlyLocalRequests and reads unchanged public fixture JSON. Separating this fixture merely to cross80 lines would make the observed request and its release barrier harder to verify.

One86-line real-browser scenario callback verifies the same uncertain preparation invariant across ordered Modules navigation, Back, deliberate reconnect, late completion, Forward/Back and a second reconnect. Parameterizing acknowledged-unknown and still-in-flight states preserves that single invariant without reconstructing durable state. URL/private-view assertions and exact query/draft/prepare/execute counts are adjacent to their transitions; fixture helpers own setup and real request completion barriers. Keeping this causal sequence together preserves test meaning better than splitting it into independently reset tests.

scope: Only two requested browser size findings; no registry mutation
